claims.text: Substituting 5–10% of Nb with V changes the electron count of NbTaHfZrTi.
The electron-count change caused by V substitution shifts the density of states at the Fermi level.
Changes in the density of states at the Fermi level modulate electron–phonon coupling strength.
Electron–phonon coupling governs superconducting pairing and Tc in this alloy.
A homogeneous, undoped NbTaHfZrTi alloy made under the same melting and cooling conditions can serve as the baseline.
Keeping casting and cooling conditions constant controls processing-related differences between the undoped and V-substituted samples.
ARPES or specific-heat measurements can be used to assess changes in the electronic density of states.
If the mechanism is correct, Tc will vary systematically with V concentration.
The V-dependent variation in Tc will correlate with corresponding changes in the density of states.
The predicted electronic and superconducting changes should occur without significant structural inhomogeneity.
The hypothesis is restricted to 5–10% V substitution when the alloy remains structurally homogeneous.
V substitution beyond the stated range could produce secondary phases.
V substitution beyond the stated range could introduce disorder effects that confound the relationship among doping, density of states, and superconductivity.
Unintentional disorder may subtly influence Tc in the proposed sample series.
Resistivity and magnetization measurements can determine Tc for the controlled sample series.
X-ray diffraction and electron microscopy can assess whether the samples remain structurally and microstructurally homogeneous.
Absence of a systematic association among V concentration, density of states, and Tc is proposed to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that structural inhomogeneity lies outside the hypothesis's valid regime and confounds interpretation, whereas the falsification rule treats detection of such inhomogeneity as falsification. A confounded or out-of-bound sample would not by itself decisively refute the proposed electronic mechanism.
